outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Controlling Generative Models
outline.description: This chapter sets the stage by introducing the power and limitations of modern text-to-image diffusion models. It defines the specific challenges of 'subject-driven' and 'controllable' generations, outlining the tension between maintaining pre-trained knowledge and acquiring new skills.
subtopics: Overview of Large Scale Text-to-Image Diffusion Models (Stable Diffusion, Imagen, etc.)
Limitations of Pure Text Guidance in Fine-Grained Control
The Core Challenge: Balancing Training Efficiency vs. Generalizability Preservation

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Foundations of Neural Network Geometry and Semantics
outline.description: Before diving into the proposed method, this chapter builds theoretical groundwork. It explores why traditional finetuning struggles to preserve semantics and introduces the concept that neuronal *angles* carry critical semantic information, whereas magnitudes are secondary.
subtopics: Critique of Traditional Gradient Descent Finetuning (Small Learning Rate Assumptions)
Euclidean Distance vs. Angular Information in Feature Spaces
Hyperspherical Representation: Normalizing Neurons to Unit Vectors
Empirical Evidence: Recovering Images from Phase/Angle Spectra Alone
Intuition from Linear Algebra: Rotating Basis Sets Without Changing Volume/Axes Relationships

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 3: Understanding Hyperspherical Energy as a Stability Metric
outline.description: This chapter delves deep into the mathematical quantity central to the paper's contribution. It explains what Hyperspherical Energy (HE) measures—specifically the pairwise relationships between neurons—and argues why preserving HE is essential for retaining pre-training capabilities.
subtopics: Mathematical Definition of Hyperspherical Energy (Summing Reciprocal Distances)

subtopics.Subtopic Name: Properties of Uniform Distribution on Hyper-Spheres
How Minimizing HE Relates to Classification vs. Generating
Heuristic Argument for Preserving Pretrained Structure
